questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=4 \\  & {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=2 \\  & {x}_{3}=-2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-2)=2\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=2+2=4.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=4$ and ${x}_{3}=-2$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-4-(-2)=4\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=4+4-2=6.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=6$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=-2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨6,4,-2⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=\frac{1}{2} \\  & y+z=1 \\  & z=2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that  $z=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get 

$$
y+2=1\,⟹\,y=1-2=-1.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=2$ and $y=-1$into the first equation to get

$$
x+(-1)+(2)=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{2}-2+1=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-\frac{1}{2}$, $y=-1$, and $z=2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨-\frac{1}{2},-1,2⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=3 \\  & {x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=\frac{1}{2} \\  & {x}_{3}=2\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}-(2)=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}+2=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{2}$ and ${x}_{3}=2$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+(\frac{5}{2})-(2)=3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=3+2-\frac{5}{2}=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{5}{2}$, ${x}_{2}=\frac{5}{2}$, and ${x}_{3}=2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨\frac{5}{2},\frac{5}{2},2⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y-z=3 \\  & y-z=2 \\  & z=1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that $z=1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y-(1)=2\,⟹\,y=2+1=3.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=1$ and $y=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
x-(3)-(1)=3\,⟹\,x=3+4=7.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=7$,  $y=3$,  and $z=1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨7,3,1⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:
    

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y-z=2 \\  & y-z=\frac{1}{2} \\  & z=3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that $z=3.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y-3=\frac{1}{2}\,⟹\,y=\frac{1}{2}+3=\frac{7}{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $y=\frac{7}{2}$ and $z=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+\frac{7}{2}-3=2\,⟹\,x=2-\frac{7}{2}+3=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=\frac{3}{2}$, $y=\frac{7}{2}$, and $z=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as
$[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{7}{2} \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+3z=-2 \\  & y+4z=0 \\  & z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $z=3.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+4(3)=0\,⟹\,y=-12.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=3$ and $y=-12$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(-12)+3(3)=-2\,⟹\,x=-2+12-9=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1$, $y=-12$, and $z=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨1,-12,3⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say,  ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=0 \\  & {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=3 \\  & {x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
{x}_{2}+(-1)=3\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=3+1=4.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=4$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}-2(4)+3(-1)=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=8+3=11.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=11$, ${x}_{2}=4$, and ${x}_{3}=-1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨11,4,-1⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 4 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say,  ${x}_{1}$, ${x}_{2}$, and ${x}_{3}.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=-3 \\  & {x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=-4 \\  & {x}_{3}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that  ${x}_{3}=-1.$ Substituting this into the second equation,  we get

$$
{x}_{2}+3(-1)=-4\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-4+3=-1.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=-1$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+(-1)+4(-1)=-3\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-3+1+4=2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is ${x}_{1}=2$, ${x}_{2}=-1$, and ${x}_{3}=-1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as
$[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=-1 \\  & y+3z=2 \\  & z=3\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $z=3.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+3(3)=2\,⟹\,y=2-9=-7.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=3$ and $y=-7$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(-7)+2(3)=-1\,⟹\,x=-1+7-6=0.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=0$, $y=-7$, and $z=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨0,-7,3⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y+z=-8 \\  & y+2z=-1 \\  & z=2\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $z=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+2(2)=-1\,⟹\,y=-1-4=-5.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=2$ and $y=-5$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+2(-5)+(2)=-8\,⟹\,x=-8+10-2=0.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=0$, $y=-5$, and $z=2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨0,-5,2⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=7 \\  & 2{x}_{3}=4\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that 

$$
2{x}_{3}=4\,⟹\,{x}_{3}=2.
$$

 Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-{x}_{2}+3(2)=7\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=6-7=-1.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+5(-1)+(2)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1+5-2=2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is 
${x}_{1}=2$, ${x}_{2}=-1$, and ${x}_{3}=2.$  In vector form, the solution can be written as $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x-2y+z=8 \\  & y-z=-1 \\  & z=0\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $z=0.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y-0=-1\,⟹\,y=-1.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=0$ and $y=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
2x-2(-1)+(0)=8\,⟹\,x=\frac{8-2}{2}=3.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=3$, $y=-1$, and $z=0.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨3,-1,0⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 2x+y-z=2 \\  & y+3z=6 \\  & -z=-3\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that

$$
-z=-3\,⟹\,z=3.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+3(3)=6\,⟹\,y=6-9=-3.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=3$ and $y=-3$ into the first equation to get 

$$
2x+(-3)-(3)=2\,⟹\,x=\frac{1}{2}(2+3+3)=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=4$, $y=-3$ and $z=3.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨4,-3,3⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+2y-z=10 \\  & y+5z=15 \\  & -z=5\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The third equation states that 

$$
-z=5\,⟹\,z=-5.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+5(-5)=15\,⟹\,y=15+25=40.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=-5$ and $y=40$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+2(40)-(-5)=10\,⟹\,x=10-80-5=-75.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-75,y=40$ and $z=-5.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as $⟨-75,40,-5⟩.$

questions.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations: 

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+z=2 \\  & 3y+2z=-1 \\  & -z=2\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that

$$
-z=2\,⟹\,z=-2.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
3y+2(-2)=-1\,⟹\,y=\frac{1}{3}(-1+4)=1.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=-2$ and $y=1$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(-2)=2\,⟹\,x=2+2=4.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=4$, $y=1$, and $z=-2.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as 
$[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$

canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y+z=3 \\ y+z=2 \\ z=2\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The third equation states that $z=2.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(2)=2 
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	y = 2-2 = 0.
$$

Now, we substitute both $z=2$ and $y=0$ into the first equation to get

$$
x+(0)+(2)=3
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x = 3-2 = 1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x = 1,$ $y=0,$ and $z = 2.$ Or, in vector form, the solution is $\langle 1,0,2 \rangle.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the system of equations that is represented by the augmented matrix

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x_1,$ $x_2,$ and $x_3.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=1 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-2 \\ {x}_{3}=5\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that $x_3=5.$ Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(5)=-2
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x_2=-2-5=-7.
$$

Now, we substitute both $x_3 = 5$ and $x_2 = -7$ into the first equation to get

$$
x_1+(-7)-(5) = 1
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x_1 = 1 + 7 + 5 = 13.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x_1 = 13,$ $x_2=-7,$ and $x_3 = 5.$ Or, in vector form, the solution is $\langle 13,-7,5 \rangle.$

canonical_examples.problem:
Solve the system of equations that is represented by the augmented matrix

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 3\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x_1,$ $x_2,$ and $x_3.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-2 \\ 3{x}_{3}=3\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that

$$
3x_3=3 
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
	x_3=1.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
x_2+(1)=-2
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x_2=-2-1=-3.
$$

Now, we substitute both $x_3 = 1$ and $x_2 = -3$ into the first equation to get

$$
2x_1+(-3)-(1) = 0
	\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
	x_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} (3 + 1) = 2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x_1 = 2,$ $x_2=-3,$ and $x_3 = 1.$ Or, in vector form, the solution is $\langle 2,-3,1 \rangle.$
